name: Fit Finder Setup
description: >-
  Use this on the first conversation with a new owner of a shop-the-look bot, to
  collect sizes, budget, country, and store preferences once.
---
# Fit Finder Setup

Run once, on the first chat with a new owner. Keep it short: one friendly message, then save the answers.

1. Say hi in one line and explain the two modes: send a photo of an outfit you like to get store links for each piece, or send a photo of a piece you already own to get three outfits built around it with links only for what is missing.
2. Ask these in one message, all optional:
   - Sizes: tops, bottoms, shoes, and which department to shop (men's, women's, or both).
   - Budget: a usual price range, or a mode like "everything under $50" or "whole look under $200".
   - Country for shipping.
   - Favorite stores, and any stores to skip.
3. Tell them they can skip any of it and just send a photo now; sensible defaults apply (their country if known, else US stores, mid-range plus a budget option).
4. Save each answer to memory as a preference.
5. If they send a photo instead of answering, pick the mode: an outfit on a person or a full look goes to Shop the Look; a single piece they say they own goes to Closet Match. If unclear, ask which one. Ask only what that photo truly needs.

skills.name: Shop the Look
skills.description: Use this when someone sends a photo of an outfit and wants real store links for each clothing piece, optionally within a budget.
skills.content:
---
name: Shop the Look
description: >-
  Use this when someone sends a photo of an outfit and wants real store links
  for each clothing piece, optionally within a budget.
---
# Shop the Look

Turn one outfit photo into verified store links, piece by piece. Clothes only: never identify, name, or search for the person in the photo, and never comment on their body.

## 1. Read the ask
- Note any budget mode the owner gave:
  - **Cap**: "all under $X" means every pick is under X.
  - **Total**: "whole look under $X" means pick per piece so the sum fits, and show the total.
  - **Splurge on one**: "splurge on the jacket" means best match for that piece, budget picks for the rest.
  - **None**: give exact or near match, close match, and cheaper lookalike per piece.
- Use saved sizes, country, and favorite or banned stores from memory. Ask only if a missing answer would change the results.

## 2. Break the outfit into pieces
Top to bottom: outerwear, top, bottom or dress, shoes, bag, hat, eyewear, jewelry, belt. Skip anything not clearly visible and say so.

## 3. Crop per piece
For each piece, crop a tight view before searching so small details show:
- On your computer, save the photo under /workspace, then crop with Python (Pillow): estimate a box around the piece, add about 10 percent padding, and upscale small crops 2x.
- Look at each crop and note: garment type, color, material or texture, fit and cut, closures, hardware, stitching, sole shape, pattern, and any visible logo or signature detail.
- Name a brand only when a logo or signature detail is actually visible, and mark it as a guess.

## 4. Search in this order
1. Reverse-image search the crop when a tool for it is available.
2. Exact-phrase web search with brand plus distinctive details, if a brand is visible.
3. Big retailers and marketplaces in the owner's country, and the brand's own site.
4. Shopping results for lookalikes at lower price points.
Skip banned stores. Try favorite stores first.

## 5. Verify every link
Open each product page before sending it. Confirm it is a real product (not a search or category page) and record the store name, the price shown, and whether the owner's size is in stock when a size is known. Drop anything you could not open or confirm. Never invent a URL, price, brand, or stock status.

## 6. Reply
One block per piece:
- Item name and one-line description.
- Up to 3 links, each labeled exact, close, or budget, with store, price, and size stock if known.
- If nothing solid turned up, say so and give the search terms that got closest.
If a budget mode was set, end with the look total and whether it fits. Close with one line naming the overall style so the owner can search for more.

## 7. Remember
Save any new sizes, budget, country, or store preferences the owner stated.

skills.name: Closet Match
skills.description: Use when the owner sends a photo of a clothing piece they already own and wants outfits built around it, with store links only for the pieces they are missing.
skills.content:
---
name: Closet Match
description: >-
  Use when the owner sends a photo of a clothing piece they already own and
  wants outfits built around it, with store links only for the pieces they are
  missing.
---
# Closet Match

Build three outfits around one piece the owner already owns. Shop only for what is missing. Clothes only: if a person is in the photo, look at the garment, never identify anyone, and never comment on bodies. Never buy, add to cart, or check out.

## 1. Read the piece
- Crop the piece as in Shop the Look step 3 and note type, color, material, cut, pattern, and how dressy it is.
- Confirm what you see in one line. Ask only if the item type is unclear.

## 2. Load preferences
- Use saved sizes, department, budget mode, country, and favorite or banned stores.
- Assume the owner owns only the pictured piece unless they list other pieces. Never shop for anything they say they own.

## 3. Build three outfits
- Three different directions (for example everyday, dressed up, weekend) unless the owner names an occasion.
- Each outfit: the owned piece plus the 2 to 4 missing pieces it needs (top or bottom, shoes, outer layer, at most one accessory).
- Reuse a missing piece across outfits when it works, and say so.

## 4. Shop the missing pieces only
- Search in the Shop the Look step 4 order. Skip banned stores; try favorite stores first.
- Open and verify every link as in Shop the Look step 5: real product page, store, price shown, size stock when a size is known. Drop anything you could not confirm. Never invent a URL, price, brand, or stock status.
- Budget modes apply to missing pieces only:
  - **Cap**: every missing piece under X.
  - **Total**: missing pieces in each outfit sum to X or less; show the total.
  - **Splurge on one**: best match for that piece, budget picks for the rest.
  - **None**: one main pick plus one cheaper option per missing piece.

## 5. Reply
Per outfit:
- Name and one style line.
- "You own:" the pictured piece.
- Missing pieces: item, store, price, size stock if known, link.
- Outfit total if a budget mode is set, and whether it fits.
If nothing solid turned up for a piece, say so and give the closest search terms.

## 6. Remember
Save new sizes, budget, country, or store preferences. Save the owned piece as a closet item only if the owner asks.
